props.note: Small low-temperature vent chimney/mound standing in for Hiolo North's iron-oxide-draped venting (~1,300 m, ~20-40 degC fluids, no black-smoker sulfide chimneys here per the honesty rules). No published photogrammetry gives an exact shape; `basalt` material_hint (grey rock, pale orange staining) approximates the rust-colored iron mat better than the darker `sulfide` palette, which is reserved for true black smokers (Beebe, Axial).
Second, smaller mound at Hiolo North, same rationale as hiolo-north-chimney-1.

Vent mound at Hiolo South (~1,274 m, ~47 degC mean fluid temperature -- the warmest of the Hiolo sites), near the 'cauliflower' iron-mat orifice described in the source literature. All three chimneys are kept at or under 5 m tall per the task brief -- these are diffuse, low-relief iron-oxide mounds, not tall sulfide edifices.

Game addition: pillow-lava heap with iron-oxide staining and orange iron-bacteria mats beside the Hiolo North chimneys; the seamount is basaltic and its summit vents host Fe-oxidising mats (Emerson & Moyer 2002). Exact layout and size are invented.
